evidence: The original extractAtDir loop had no `--` check, so `lit ls -- --at /p` routed to a foreign store; 3a71e21 adds `if args[i] == "--" { return "", false }` plus a direct unit test. Declining the residual other-flag-value collision is sound, since solving it would need a second copy of the ls flagset's arities.
guidance_note: When writing a pre-parse routing scan over argv, enumerate the parser's own terminators and flag-shaped-value cases (`--`, `--x --help`, `--x=`) in the first test table before the reviewer does.

evidence: familyCmd called runWithApp before any subcommand handler, so the hidden `bulk import` pointer was masked by the outside-workspace error; the original test used runAppFamily with a nil app and skipped that path. 3a71e21 adds a skipApp row field and drives the real `Run` from a non-repo cwd.
guidance_note: When adding a retirement pointer, test it through the production dispatch entry point (`Run`) from a non-workspace cwd, the same way the top-level retirements are reachable, not through a helper that bypasses the app open.

evidence: The CHANGELOG announced `lit stores --counts` while docs/cli-reference.md had no `lit stores` section; 3a71e21 adds one covering the default listing, --counts, and the store-intrinsic readiness caveat.
guidance_note: When a CHANGELOG entry names a flag on a command, grep the CLI reference for that command's section and add it in the same commit if it is missing.

evidence: The reference still documented `lit ready`/`lit queue` with full synopses although the CHANGELOG called them retired. The fix was right in kind, but the heading it wrote, "`lit queue` (retired → `lit backlog`)", misstated the shared pointer and drew F6.
guidance_note: When writing a doc line that describes a code-emitted message, copy the target list from the constant (`workableRetirementGuidance`) rather than paraphrasing it.

evidence: With only an empty-string check, `lit ls --at --help` handed "--help" to OpenLocationForRead; 3a71e21 adds `strings.HasPrefix(atDir, "-")` to the usage-error guard, and TestLsAtRejectsEmptyOrFlagShapedDir covers `--at --help`, `--at --status`, and `--at=--nope`.
guidance_note: When rejecting an empty flag value, also reject a flag-shaped value in the same guard; both mean the value token is missing.

evidence: The F4 fix commit 3a71e21 wrote the heading "`lit ready` (retired → `lit backlog` / `lit next`) and `lit queue` (retired → `lit backlog`)", while both commands share workableRetirementGuidance, which names backlog and next. The doc text the fix added contradicted the code; 41a738f merged them into one heading.
guidance_note: When the fix is a doc line describing code output, read the emitting constant and quote its targets verbatim instead of paraphrasing per command.

narrative: Round 0 found five real issues: two extractAtDir routing edge cases, a retirement pointer that was unreachable outside a workspace, and two doc gaps. All were accepted and fixed in one commit, 3a71e21. That commit's new retired-commands heading paraphrased the shared retirement pointer wrongly, which cost round 1 (F6). Round 2 was clean.
guidance_observations: The original test for the bulk import retirement used a helper that bypassed the very dispatch step that was broken; testing through the production entry point would have caught F2 before review.
Bundling all five round-0 fixes into one commit with targeted tests kept the cycle short; the one leak was a hand-paraphrased doc heading.

evidence: The agent confirmed that LoadWithSource/ActiveOverride now resolve quickstart-work.md and that `--refresh` iterates only managed names, so an old-named override is invisible. It chose one of the reviewer's two offered options, a CHANGELOG migration line, on the epic constraint that breaks be "deliberate and documented". At runtime the override is still ignored silently, but advisory severity and the absence of any orphan-override detector make the documented break defensible.
guidance_note: When renaming a user-overridable template file, decide in the original PR how an override left at the old name gets surfaced (a CHANGELOG migration line at minimum) instead of leaving it to the reviewer.

narrative: This was a guidance-sync rename of the quickstart topic from ready to work. The one inline finding was the silently orphaned old-name override, which the agent resolved with a documented-break CHANGELOG line. Both round summaries also flagged an out-of-diff stale `ready`/`queue`/`next` triple at docs/cli-reference.md:245 (the `focus` label text), which the agent never addressed before merge.
guidance_observations: Summary-only findings outside the diff (cli-reference.md:245, flagged in both rounds) went unaddressed because no inline thread carried them; the reply process should sweep round summaries as well as threads.
A rename PR whose purpose is to remove retired command names should grep the whole docs tree for those names, not only the files it touched.

evidence: A `{when: enter}` mapping unmarshalled to State="" and compactStates dropped it with no warning. In 428a610 UnmarshalYAML returns "state entry mapping requires a non-empty name", which refuses the illegal shape at the parse boundary, and the malformed-table test covers it.
guidance_note: When a compaction step drops empty entries, check whether an authored structured entry (a mapping) can reach it empty, and reject that shape at unmarshal.

evidence: The CHANGELOG said the default id is "the file's relative path", but defaultID drops `.md` and replaces spaces with underscores; 428a610 rewords it to match.
guidance_note: When a CHANGELOG describes a derived value, read the deriving function and state each transformation it applies.

evidence: Flagged ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT 428a610, but that commit touched only state-mapping rejection and the CHANGELOG. The flagged code, `toEvents(compactStrings(meta.Events))` with trim and no lowercase, is unchanged from the original PR, so the flag is a false positive. The premise holds: catalog names are lowercase, so `Show_Ticket` would warn and never match.
guidance_note: When canonicalizing one dimension of a multi-dimension schema (labels lowercased), apply the same canonical form to every sibling dimension and enum field in the same commit.

evidence: The F3 fix adf3e95 lowercased events "symmetric with label canonicalization" but left state names (`strings.TrimSpace(node.Value)`) case-sensitive, although Occasion states come from the lifecycle in lowercase. It was the same case-canonicalization gap in the next dimension of the same file, which a982625 then fixed.
guidance_note: When a fix's own justification is 'symmetric with X', list every sibling field the symmetry argument covers (labels, events, states, when) and fix them all in that commit.

evidence: The F4 fix a982625 added canonicalState and its comment declared lowercasing "the one convention shared by all three activation dimensions", yet parseWhen, a few lines away in the same UnmarshalYAML arm, still compared `When(strings.TrimSpace(raw))` case-sensitively. It was a third instance of the same gap; d4f6479 lowercased it.
guidance_note: After declaring a convention in a comment ('every frontmatter field is case-insensitive'), grep every parse function in the file for the comparison it should now apply before pushing.

evidence: Flagged ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT d4f6479, which touched only parseWhen. splitFrontmatter's `strings.TrimRight(firstLine, "\r")` is original PR code, so the flag is a false positive. The premise holds: `--- ` silently loses all frontmatter. Factoring both delimiter checks into one isDelimiter predicate is an apt one-source-of-truth use.
guidance_note: When tolerating one trailing-character variant on a delimiter line (\r), tolerate the whole class (trailing horizontal whitespace) through one shared predicate used by both open and close checks.

narrative: Round 0 found a silent drop of nameless state mappings and a CHANGELOG imprecision; both were fixed correctly. Round 1 raised event-case asymmetry against original code. The agent fixed events only, which led round 2 to find the same gap in states; fixing states then led round 3 to find it in `when:`. Each fix argued symmetry but swept one more field instead of all of them. Round 4's delimiter-whitespace finding was unrelated original code.
guidance_observations: Three consecutive rounds were spent on one canonicalization gap, one field at a time; the first fix should have enumerated every authored field in the frontmatter struct and applied the convention to all.
Each agent reply named the symmetry principle explicitly, so the information needed to sweep was already in hand; the missing move was listing the fields the principle covered.

evidence: The agent states that Store.Apply runs UpdateIssueInput.Labels through canonicalizeLabels -> model.NormalizeLabel (trim, lowercase, dedupe), the same path `lit update --labels` uses. Review summaries in #345 independently say store/labels.go delegates to model.NormalizeLabel at canonicalizeLabels. This packet does not show the store.go lines themselves, but the claim is corroborated, and a second trim would duplicate the single enforcer.

The agent verified that Reason is not normalized in the store (assigned verbatim to the event) while runUpdate trims it at the CLI boundary; c596936 trims it in bulkUpdateChange, and a CLI test pins it.
guidance_note: When building a second entry point that mirrors an existing command's field assembly (`lit update`), diff it field by field against that command's boundary normalization, noting which fields the store normalizes and which the caller must.

evidence: registerActor added `--by` to the shared import flagset, but the JSON branch never called resolveActor, so a previously rejected flag became a silent no-op; c596936 rejects `fs.Changed("by")` on the JSON branch. The fix covered only the JSON branch, and the create-only YAML case resurfaced as F7.
guidance_note: When registering a flag on a command with several dispatch branches, list every branch (including YAML files with no update documents) and decide for each whether it consumes the flag.

evidence: Flagged ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT c596936, which only changed the Reason line in bulkUpdateChange. The `v, _ := model.ParseIssueType` discards are original PR code, so the flag is a false positive. The premise is latent, not an active bug, but the agent rightly noted that the sibling create branch already propagates these same errors, so matching it was consistent.
guidance_note: When a function re-parses already-validated input, follow the convention its sibling branch uses (propagate the error) rather than discarding with `_`.

evidence: This duplicates F4 on the same two lines and was fixed by the same 02980a4 change to `(Change, error)`. The flag is a false positive for the same reason as F4: the discards predate c596936.

Flagged ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT c596936, which did not touch docs; the "plus `reason` ... At least one of those fields" text is from the original PR, so the flag is a false positive. bulkUpdateHasField excludes reason, so the doc was ambiguous-to-wrong, and 02980a4 rewords it.
guidance_note: When documenting an 'at least one of' rule, list exactly the fields the predicate counts and name any excluded field separately.

evidence: The F3 fix c596936 rejected an unused `--by` only on the JSON branch, while BulkApply consumes actor only in bulkUpdateChange, so a create-only YAML file silently discarded `--by` too. The agent's reply says "this is the same class of gap the previous round's --by fix closed on the JSON side"; 35c5dda adds a bulkSpecsHaveUpdate rejection.
guidance_note: When closing a 'flag silently discarded' finding, trace every path to the flag's single consumer and reject wherever that consumer is not reached, not only on the branch the reviewer named.

evidence: Flagged ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT 35c5dda, which touched only CLI `--by` handling. `Placement: RankBottom` is original PR code, so the flag is a false positive. The two formats of one command did rank creates oppositely, undocumented; the agent aligned YAML with JSON's RankTop and declined a mode flag, a defensible one-behavior choice, though it gives up the file-order preservation the agent originally intended.
guidance_note: When a new format joins an existing command, diff its create inputs (placement, actor, defaults) against the existing format's and either match them or document the difference in the original PR.

evidence: Flagged ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT 35c5dda, which did not touch the CHANGELOG; the "dispatched by the `.json` extension" wording is from the original PR, so the flag is a false positive. The dispatch is a default branch for any non-yaml extension, as the CLI reference already said; 8106194 rewords it.
guidance_note: When the CHANGELOG and the reference describe the same dispatch rule, write one from the other so they cannot disagree.

narrative: The YAML bulk import drew nine findings across four rounds with findings. One pushback (label trimming, F1) was correct, since the store already canonicalizes labels. Most later findings were anchored to fix commits but sat on original code: the error discards, reason docs, RankBottom placement, and CHANGELOG dispatch wording. The one real fix-caused finding was F7: the `--by` rejection added for JSON missed create-only YAML files, which cost round 2.
guidance_observations: Many ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flags here were anchoring artifacts on original code; the PR's real cost was an original diff that never compared the new format's behavior field by field against the existing JSON format and `lit update`.
The agent's reply to F7 recognized it as the same gap class as F3; sweeping every dispatch branch at F3 time would have removed a round.

evidence: The rewrite removed "do NOT ignore" from firstPushSkipMessage, leaving `strings.Contains(got, "do NOT ignore") || ...` with a dead first branch. The reviewer said it was "permanently true", but it is actually permanently false; either way the assertion was weakened, and 60af926 pins the new phrasing.
guidance_note: When rewording a string constant, grep the tests for every old substring and update each assertion in the same commit.

evidence: The touched error text says "embedded dolt pull" while the function comment says "Adopt now CLONES" and the call is store.AdoptRemoteByClone; 60af926 fixes both messages.
guidance_note: When rewriting a message's phrasing, re-verify its factual claims against the code it describes, not only its tone.

narrative: This was a text-only rephrasing of agent guidance away from ALL-CAPS imperatives. Round 0 found a dead test assertion left by the reworded constant and a stale pull/clone term in rewritten error text; both were fixed in one commit. Round 1 approved, but its summary noted a remaining stale "MUST-NOT-IGNORE directive" code comment at prose_pending.go:71, which the agent did not address.
guidance_observations: A phrasing sweep should grep code comments and tests for the old phrases, not only user-facing strings; both leftovers here were references to the old wording.
A summary-only note (prose_pending.go:71) went unaddressed because it had no inline thread.

evidence: The added code's own comment admitted that AddComment "already validated exists" before a second GetIssue call. 0c031f0 returns the internally read issue from AddComment, and the round-1 summary confirms all callers were updated.
guidance_note: When a comment has to explain why a second read of the same row is needed, return the first read from the function that performed it instead.

narrative: This PR wired semantic event dispatch into every curated command. The single finding was a redundant issue fetch in runCommentAdd, which the agent fixed by widening AddComment's return. Round 1 approved with no inline findings.

evidence: The Unreleased section carried two groundwork bullets saying "Not yet wired" / "Still no observable effect" next to a new "`lit workflows` is live" bullet; bfd2ffd consolidates them into one end-state entry.
guidance_note: When a ticket completes a feature whose earlier tickets left 'not yet' entries in the same Unreleased section, rewrite those entries into the end state in the same PR.

evidence: Flagged ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT bfd2ffd, which changed only the CHANGELOG; Dispatch's handling of set.Warnings is original PR code, so the flag is a false positive. Warnings were in fact never surfaced and the comment overclaimed, so the agent corrected the comment and deferred display to ffqz.4. #357 (ffqz.4) delivered that surface with malformed-file warning tests, which confirms the deferral was real and not a dodge.
guidance_note: When a doc comment describes data as 'not discarded' because a future surface will read it, state the gap and the ticket that closes it in the original PR.

evidence: This duplicates F2 on the same line and got the same disposition and fix (6715800, a comment rewrite). The flag is a false positive because bfd2ffd touched only the CHANGELOG. Writing warnings to `w` would inject config diagnostics into every command's agent-facing stdout, so rejecting that cure was right.

Flagged ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT 6715800, which touched only dispatch.go's comment. The backtick "`lit workflows` is live" wording was already in the original round-0 CHANGELOG line and in cli-reference.md, so the flag is a false positive. No `workflows` command was registered at that point, so the quoting implied a nonexistent command.
guidance_note: In CLI docs, backtick a `lit <word>` phrase only when it is a registered command; refer to a feature by plain name until its command ships.

narrative: Round 0 found contradictory CHANGELOG entries, which were consolidated. Round 1 raised duplicate findings that Dispatch discarded Set.Warnings while its comment claimed otherwise. The agent kept the diagnosis, corrected the comment, and deferred display to ffqz.4, which #357 delivered. Round 2 caught command-implying backticks that were in the original text. No finding was caused by a fix.
guidance_observations: The agent's different_fix on the warnings thread was well-founded: it rejected the reviewer's cure of writing to the command's stdout while honoring the diagnosis, and the follow-up ticket actually shipped the surface.

evidence: runWorkflows calls `splitArgs(args, 2)` and parseFlagSet with no `fs.NArg() != 0` check, so `show my-id extra junk` silently ignores the overflow, unlike every other splitArgs caller the reviewer listed; 7981a0e adds the check and a regression test.
guidance_note: When adding a command that uses a shared arg-splitting helper, copy the full validation idiom its existing callers use (`fs.NArg() != 0` -> UsageError), not just the split call.

narrative: This PR added the `lit workflows` see-it surface. The one finding was a missing oversupplied-argument check that every sibling command has; it was fixed with a regression test, and round 1 approved.
